Maneuvering

Impulso de Potencia Incremental

A technique involving small, timed increases in engine or thruster power to control a vessel’s position or heading precisely during docking or undocking.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Impulso de Potencia Incremental?

In this glossary, Impulso de Potencia Incremental refers to: A technique involving small, timed increases in engine or thruster power to control a vessel’s position or heading precisely during docking or undocking.

How is Impulso de Potencia Incremental used in maritime?

In maritime communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Utilice impulsos de potencia incremental para contrarrestar la deriva y mantener el alineamiento con el muelle durante el atraque."

Why does Impulso de Potencia Incremental matter in maritime?

Impulso de Potencia Incremental matters because it supports clear communication in Maneuvering contexts for Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as STCW, Marlins Test, ISF Watchkeeper, and GMDSS.

Who uses Impulso de Potencia Incremental?

Impulso de Potencia Incremental is mainly used by Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters.

Definition

A technique involving small, timed increases in engine or thruster power to control a vessel’s position or heading precisely during docking or undocking.

Operational example

Use incremental power bursts to counteract drift and maintain vessel alignment with the quay during docking.

Localized term

Impulso de Potencia Incremental

Localized example

Utilice impulsos de potencia incremental para contrarrestar la deriva y mantener el alineamiento con el muelle durante el atraque.
